headline: A preprint defines a Fisher leverage measure for comparing language-model weight updates
summary: An October 27 arXiv preprint introduces leverage, the Fisher quadratic form of a weight update divided by the same form for a random direction of equal size at the same checkpoint. Across released Olmo-3, Tülu-3, Zephyr and OLMo-2 checkpoints, the author reports leverage near 1 for two pretraining windows on a 51,167-token mixed corpus, about 5 for SFT, hundreds to low thousands for RL-Zero/RLVR, and values from hundreds to tens of thousands for DPO. Controlled training and one released OLMo-2 DPO recipe rerun support some of the reported contrasts. The paper also reports that a sign-structure term predicts damage from random delta sparsification in tested cases. These are author-reported research results. The metric measures local next-token distribution change, not task capability; results are bounded by the corpora and training regimes studied, and no independent reproduction was performed here.
